$comment: TASK-861 — the ResolvedAsrSpec cross-language contract fixture. `input` is what TASK-863's AgentResolverService returns (a ResolvedAgent, plus the resolved `parameters.fallback.agentSlug` agent when one is named); `expected` is what `buildResolvedAsrSpec()` (@arcaai/applications) MUST produce from it and what `apps/stt/src/stt/pipeline/spec.py` MUST validate and map. Both `tests/contracts/resolved-asr-spec-parity.contract.test.ts` and `apps/stt/tests/unit/test_resolved_spec_parity.py` read this file; change it with both suites open. TASK-977 — every audio front-end STAGE is now a declared agent opinion, OFF by default: `vad.enabled` is read from the agent (it used to be the literal `true`), `denoise.enabled` is declared rather than inferred from a bound model, and a stage the spec ships as OFF ships no model for it, so `apps/stt` warms none. `resample`/`normalize` are NOT stages and stay `true`. The cases below cover both polarities: `platformDefault` runs VAD on a bound model, `twoConnectionsOfOneVendor` denoises on a bound model, and `cloudWithAgentFallback` binds a denoise model with the stage off.

platformDefault.$comment: The SYSTEM `platform-transcription` agent: GGUF whisper primary, Silero VAD, ECAPA diarization, one AgentModelFallback row (kind: model). TASK-880 — both ASR rows carry `AiModel._metadata.asr` decode geometry, which travels as `models.asr.metadata`: the whisper.cpp primary declares the 7s decode window and the 6s partial tail that used to be the platform keys `stt.whisperCpp.maxAudioSeconds` / `stt.streaming.partialWindowS`, and the CT2 fallback declares its OWN 30s window — which is the point of moving them onto the row. The other two cases omit `metadata` entirely. TASK-934 adds `decoding.sources`: the row declares the 6s partial tail, so `partialWindowSec: 'model'`; the agent declares beamSize, the prompt and the hotwords, so those read 'agent'. TASK-977 — `audioFrontEnd.vad.enabled` is declared `true` here, which is what keeps `models.vad` in the spec; this is the fixture’s positive VAD path. The SEEDED agent ships it `false` (owner decision D-1) — a contract fixture pins the SHAPE of an enabled stage, not the seed’s choice.

cloudWithAgentFallback.$comment: A tenant agent on a cloud (Azure) row with a denoise model and a `fallback.agentSlug` naming a second published agent (kind: agent). Credentials are NOT here — they travel as provider_overrides. TASK-977 — this agent binds a denoise model but never declares `denoise.enabled`, so the stage is OFF (`level: "off"`) and `models.denoise` is NOT shipped. That is the regression this ticket fixed: enablement used to be derived from the binding, so attaching a row to inspect it switched noise suppression on.

agentOwnedStreamingBehaviour.$comment: TASK-877 — the fields the runtime used to DROP. A tenant agent that asks for semantic endpointing, tunes it, binds an `endpointing` (end-of-utterance) model, sets its own partial cadence and utterance cap, turns the engine's own `vadFilter` on, and sets per-agent batch chunking. Every one of these replaced a platform key that TASK-877 deleted (`stt.streaming.partialIntervalS`, `stt.semanticEndpoint.*`). The three additive wire fields — `decoding.{chunkLengthSec,strideLengthSec}` and `streaming.semantic` — are OPTIONAL: the other two cases omit them entirely, which is what keeps the two halves deployable in either order against `extra='forbid'`. TASK-880 adds `audioFrontEnd.vad.speechPadMs`, which replaces the platform key `stt.vad.speechPadMs` and follows the same omit-when-absent rule — the other two cases set no padding, so the key is absent from their `audioFrontEnd.vad` blocks entirely.

modelProfileDecodeKnobs.$comment: TASK-934 — the per-model ASR decode profile. The q8_0 ml-en fine-tune's row carries a FULL `_metadata.asr` profile (both windows, the six previously-hardcoded decode knobs, its priming prompt and its hotwords); the tenant agent overrides `beamSize`, `noSpeechThreshold` and — OD-4 — the partial window, and says nothing else. Expected shows the OD-3 fold: agent wins where it spoke, the row fills the rest, `decoding.sources` names the tier per knob, and `models.asr.metadata` keeps the row's raw recommendation as provenance (note `partialWindowSec` there is the EFFECTIVE 15, not the row's 6 — it rides where apps/stt already reads it). The other three cases carry NONE of these keys, which is what keeps the two halves deployable in either order against `extra='forbid'`. TASK-946 (OD-1) adds `decoding.hotwordsInPrompt`, folded by the same two-tier rule and reported in `sources`: this row declares it ON, so the whisper.cpp adapter may append its hotwords to the decoder prompt. `clinicalVocabularyCorrection` carries the SAME row WITHOUT the key on purpose — that is the absent case, where the terms still reach the lexicon stage and the prompt is left alone.

asr.initialPrompt: Clinical consultation between a clinician and a patient. English and Malayalam medical terminology.

metadata.initialPrompt: Clinical consultation between a clinician and a patient. English and Malayalam medical terminology.

instruction.initialPrompt: Clinical consultation between a clinician and a patient. English and Malayalam medical terminology.

clinicalVocabularyCorrection.$comment: TASK-935 (OD-2 a / OD-5 a) — the clinical-vocabulary correction stage on the wire. The agent declares postProcessing.lexicon { enabled, maxDistance }; the TERMS are NOT here, because they are instruction.hotwords — one list, two consumers (decoder prompt bias since TASK-934, and this stage). This case deliberately takes the hotwords from the MODEL row (decoding.sources.hotwords: 'model') while the stage itself is the agent's choice, which is the combination that would break if either side ever grew its own term list. Every OTHER case omits `lexicon` entirely — the omit-when-absent rule, which is what lets the two halves deploy in either order against an extra='forbid' mirror.

asr.initialPrompt: Clinical consultation between a clinician and a patient. English and Malayalam medical terminology.

metadata.initialPrompt: Clinical consultation between a clinician and a patient. English and Malayalam medical terminology.

instruction.initialPrompt: Clinical consultation between a clinician and a patient. English and Malayalam medical terminology.

twoConnectionsOfOneVendor.$comment: TASK-958 D-3/D-4 — a tenant holding TWO accounts of one vendor. The primary and the model-level fallback name the SAME engine (`azure-speech`) on DIFFERENT connections, so each core carries its own `connectionId`/`connectionSlug`/`connectionKey` and `apps/stt` reads each chain's credential under its own key instead of handing both the entry that just failed. Every other example is untouched and carries none of the three fields, which is what pins them as omit-when-absent.
